source_meta._title: Item entities' health does not decrease uniformly when on cacti

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 26.1 Snapshot 9 in a fresh single-player Superflat world, using Creative mode with commands/cheats enabled. The test uses one item entity, a cactus at X=0, Y=200, Z=0, and an observation platform four blocks away.
preconditions: The exact affected version, 26.1 Snapshot 9, is installed and launchable.
The executor can create a single-player world with commands/cheats enabled.
Command feedback is visible in chat so that summon, tick, and entity-data command responses can be recorded.
Use a fresh world and do not drop or summon any other item entities near the test area; the health selector must resolve only the test item.
Keep the game frozen except when executing the three explicit five-tick steps. Do not unfreeze the game with /tick unfreeze.

steps.action: Launch Minecraft Java Edition using the exact affected version 26.1 Snapshot 9. Do not use the listed fix version, 26.1 Pre-Release 2.
steps.success_cue: The title screen identifies the running game version as 26.1 Snapshot 9.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set the game mode to Creative, enable commands/cheats, select the Superflat world type, and create the world. The Superflat selection is only to provide a predictable empty test area.
steps.success_cue: The player is in a newly created Creative-mode Superflat world and can open chat and execute commands.

steps.action: Wait until world loading has finished before starting the test. Do not leave dropped items near the player.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain is rendered, player movement responds normally, and no item entities are visible near the player.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat, enter the freeze command with its leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Chat confirms that the game is frozen. Commands can still be entered, but normal game ticks no longer advance continuously.

steps.action: While the game remains frozen, press T, enter the teleport command, and press Enter. This moves the player to the center of the block at X=0, Y=200, Z=0, safely above the Superflat terrain.
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary at approximately X=0.5, Y=200, Z=0.5 and does not fall because ticking is frozen.

steps.action: Press T, place a sand support block directly beneath the planned cactus position by executing the command, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback confirms that a sand block exists at X=0, Y=199, Z=0.

steps.action: Press T, place the cactus directly at the player's current block position by executing the command, and press Enter. The cactus is therefore directly above the sand support.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback confirms that a cactus block exists at X=0, Y=200, Z=0, supported by the sand at Y=199.

steps.action: Press T, place a separate standing platform four blocks east of the cactus by executing the command, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: A stone block exists at X=4, Y=199, Z=0, within five blocks of the cactus but not adjacent to it.

steps.action: While still positioned inside the cactus block and while the game remains frozen, press T and execute the report's item summon command exactly as shown, including the leading slash and NBT data.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback confirms that an item entity was summoned at the player's position inside the cactus. No game ticks have elapsed since it was summoned.

steps.action: Press T and teleport to the center of the observation platform. This prevents the player from remaining inside the cactus while keeping the item within the health command's five-block selector range.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing on the stone platform approximately four blocks from the cactus, and the game is still frozen.

steps.action: Before advancing any ticks, press T and execute the report's health query. Press Enter and record the complete chat response as the cumulative-tick-0 measurement. Do not evaluate whether the value is correct.
steps.exact_input: /execute as @e[type=item,distance=..5] run data get entity @s Health
steps.success_cue: A health query response for the single nearby item entity is visible and has been recorded as the tick-0 measurement.

steps.action: Press T and advance the frozen game by exactly five ticks using the report's tick-step command. Press Enter, then wait until all five requested ticks have completed and command input is responsive again. Do not run /tick unfreeze.
steps.success_cue: Exactly five ticks have been requested and completed; the game has returned to its frozen state at cumulative tick 5.

steps.action: Press T and run the same health query again. Record the complete command response as the cumulative-tick-5 measurement without interpreting it. If the selector reports no matching entity, record that exact response instead of summoning a replacement.
steps.exact_input: /execute as @e[type=item,distance=..5] run data get entity @s Health
steps.success_cue: The tick-5 query response, whether entity data or no-matching-entity feedback, has been recorded, and no replacement item has been created.

steps.action: Press T and advance the game by another five ticks. Wait until the requested ticks finish and the game is frozen again.
steps.success_cue: A second group of exactly five ticks has completed, bringing the cumulative stepped time to 10 ticks.

steps.action: Press T and run the same health query. Record the complete response as the cumulative-tick-10 measurement without interpreting it. If no entity matches, preserve that command response and continue without summoning another item.
steps.exact_input: /execute as @e[type=item,distance=..5] run data get entity @s Health
steps.success_cue: The tick-10 query response has been recorded, and the test still refers to the originally summoned item rather than a replacement.

steps.action: Press T and advance the game by a third and final group of exactly five ticks. Wait until command processing is responsive and the game has returned to its frozen state.
steps.success_cue: The third five-tick step has completed, bringing the cumulative stepped time to 15 ticks while leaving the game frozen.

steps.action: Press T and run the health query one final time. Record the complete response as the cumulative-tick-15 measurement. Do not summon another item if the selector no longer finds the original entity, and do not evaluate the collected measurements.
steps.exact_input: /execute as @e[type=item,distance=..5] run data get entity @s Health
steps.success_cue: The tick-15 command response has been captured alongside the previously recorded tick-0, tick-5, and tick-10 responses.

stor.handoff_condition: The originally summoned item has undergone three consecutive five-tick advances while in contact with the cactus, for 15 cumulative stepped ticks. The world is frozen again, and the unaltered command responses from cumulative ticks 0, 5, 10, and 15 have been recorded for the observation subsystem to evaluate.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode, world seed, world type, or single-player versus dedicated-server environment. This plan uses a fresh Creative-mode single-player Superflat world with commands enabled as the simplest deterministic implementation.

The report does not provide fixed coordinates or a complete cactus layout. The plan uses a sand-supported cactus at X=0, Y=200, Z=0 and summons the item from the center of that cactus block, matching the report's instruction that the item be directly inside or otherwise in contact with the cactus.

The sand, cactus, observation platform, and teleport commands are practical setup choices and are not commands supplied by the report. The report-supplied summon, health-query, freeze, and tick-step command text is preserved.

The report describes repeating the health-check and five-tick-step sequence multiple times, with up to 15 total ticks as its example. This plan deterministically performs exactly three five-tick advances for 15 cumulative ticks.

source_meta.issue links: Duplicate:inward:MC-306642:almost every Enderman that spawns is holding nothing | Duplicate:inward:MC-306651:All endermen appear to be holding a block, even when not
source_meta._title: Endermen now display the block-holding pose even when empty-handed

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 26.1 Snapshot 10 in a single-player Creative-mode world, with commands/cheats enabled, difficulty set to Normal (or another non-Peaceful difficulty), and the test area set to nighttime so the Enderman is not exposed to daylight.
preconditions: Launch exactly Minecraft Java Edition 26.1 Snapshot 10, the first and only version listed as affected in the report. Do not use the fixed version, 26.1 Snapshot 11.
Use a newly created or otherwise disposable world in Creative mode so an Enderman Spawn Egg can be obtained without exploration or combat.
Enable commands/cheats for the world so nighttime can be established deterministically.
Use a non-Peaceful difficulty because hostile mobs, including Endermen, may not remain present on Peaceful difficulty.
Use the normal game resources for the test; avoid optional resource packs or modifications that intentionally replace the Enderman model or animations.
After spawning the Enderman, proceed immediately to observation without giving it time to collect a nearby block.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation for Minecraft Java Edition version 26.1 Snapshot 10, then launch it. On the title screen, verify that the displayed version is 26.1 Snapshot 10 before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft title screen is open and identifies the running version as 26.1 Snapshot 10.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, then Create New World. Set the game mode to Creative, set difficulty to Normal or another non-Peaceful difficulty, and ensure commands/cheats are enabled. No particular seed, world type, or coordinates are required by the report. Create the world.
steps.success_cue: A new Creative-mode world begins loading with commands available and difficulty not set to Peaceful.

steps.action: Wait for the world to finish loading. Do not continue until nearby terrain is rendered, the player can look and move normally, and inventory or chat inputs respond without initial loading delay.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in the loaded world and normal movement and input are responsive.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat. Type the time command exactly as shown, including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The sky changes to nighttime and the command completes without an error message.

steps.action: Press E, or the currently bound Inventory control, to open the Creative inventory. Open the Search Items tab, select the search field, and enter the exact item name shown.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory search results include an Enderman Spawn Egg.

steps.action: Move one Enderman Spawn Egg from the search results into an empty slot in the hotbar, which is the row of nine item slots at the bottom of the inventory. Close the inventory with E or Esc.
steps.success_cue: The inventory is closed and an Enderman Spawn Egg is visible in one of the nine hotbar slots.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing the Enderman Spawn Egg, using its number key or the mouse wheel. Stand in an open area and aim the crosshair at a ground block approximately 4 to 6 blocks away so the spawned Enderman's full body can be viewed without the player standing inside it.
steps.success_cue: The Enderman Spawn Egg is shown in the player's hand and the crosshair points at nearby unobstructed ground during nighttime.

steps.action: Right-click once, or use the currently bound Use Item/Place Block control once, on the targeted ground block to spawn a fresh Enderman. Do not use the spawn egg a second time, attack the Enderman, place a block in its hands, or wait for it to collect a block.
steps.success_cue: Exactly one newly spawned Enderman is visible near the player and is unobstructed enough for its complete model and arm position to be inspected.

stor.handoff_condition: A fresh Enderman has just been spawned from an Enderman Spawn Egg in Minecraft Java Edition 26.1 Snapshot 10 during nighttime. No carried block was assigned as part of the setup, and the player has not attacked or otherwise interacted with it. Begin model-pose observation immediately, before the Enderman can collect a block or leave the viewing area.
uncertainties: The report contains no formal Steps to Reproduce, seed, coordinates, game mode, or required world configuration. The plan therefore reconstructs the minimum deterministic path implied by the description: create a fresh Enderman and inspect it while it has not been given time to collect a block.
Using Creative mode and an Enderman Spawn Egg is an execution choice, not a requirement stated by the report.
The plan treats a freshly created Enderman from the standard spawn egg as initially empty-handed. The report does not provide an NBT or data-command check for the carried-block state.

Nighttime and a non-Peaceful difficulty are used to keep the Enderman available for inspection; the report states that the behavior occurs under any circumstances and does not identify either setting as a required trigger.

source_meta._title: Sulfur cubes with TNT absorbed still explode with the game rule `mob_griefing` set to false

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft: Java Edition 26.2 Snapshot 5 in a single-player Creative-mode world using the integrated server. Enable commands/cheats when creating the world. Use an isolated snapshot installation and a disposable test world; do not use the listed fix version, 26.2 Snapshot 6. A default or flat world is acceptable because the report supplies no seed, coordinates, structure, biome, graphics setting, or dedicated-server requirement.
preconditions: Minecraft: Java Edition 26.2 Snapshot 5 is installed and selected in the Minecraft Launcher.
The client is unmodified: no mods, custom datapacks, or server plugins are active.
A disposable single-player world can be created in Creative mode with commands enabled.
Use the bound controls for Open Chat, Use Item/Place Block, and Inventory; their default keyboard-and-mouse inputs are T, right-click, and E respectively.
The test area must contain a solid, open surface where a Sulfur Cube can be spawned and approached without falling into a hazard.
Do not perform this reproduction in 26.2 Snapshot 6, because the report lists that version as the fix version.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, start the installation whose version is exactly 26.2 Snapshot 5. At the title screen, confirm that the displayed version is 26.2 Snapshot 5 before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft: Java Edition title screen is open and identifies the running version as 26.2 Snapshot 5.

steps.action: Create a new disposable single-player world. Set Game Mode to Creative and ensure commands/cheats are enabled. The report does not require a particular seed or world type, so use the default world settings or a flat world for easier testing.
steps.success_cue: The player has entered a newly created Creative-mode world and is permitted to execute commands.

steps.action: Wait before setting up the test. Do not continue until nearby terrain has rendered, the player can move normally, and opening menus or chat responds without world-loading delay. Move to a clear solid surface if the initial position is obstructed or hazardous.
steps.success_cue: The surrounding chunks are rendered, controls respond normally, and there is a clear solid surface near the player.

steps.action: Press T, or the rebound Open Chat control, to open chat. Enter the game-rule command exactly as supplied in exact_input, including the leading slash, and press Enter. The namespaced snake_case rule name is appropriate for this affected version.
steps.success_cue: The command succeeds and the game reports that the minecraft:mob_griefing game rule is now false.

steps.action: Verify the game-rule state immediately before constructing the trigger. Open chat, enter the query command exactly as supplied in exact_input, including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The command output reports that minecraft:mob_griefing is false. Do not continue if it reports true or if the command fails.

steps.action: Press E, or the rebound Inventory control, to open the Creative inventory. Use the inventory search field to locate the Sulfur Cube Spawn Egg, TNT, and Flint and Steel. Place each item into a separate hotbar slot; the hotbar is the row of nine quickly selectable slots at the bottom of the inventory and gameplay screen. Close the inventory when all three items are present.
steps.success_cue: The hotbar contains a Sulfur Cube Spawn Egg, TNT, and Flint and Steel in separate slots.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing the Sulfur Cube Spawn Egg, aim the crosshair at the clear solid surface, and press Use Item/Place Block once; the default input is right-click. Keep the spawned cube in view.
steps.success_cue: One living Sulfur Cube is visible on the test surface near the player.

steps.action: Select the TNT item in the hotbar. Stand within interaction range, aim the crosshair directly at the Sulfur Cube rather than at the ground behind it, and press Use Item once; the default input is right-click. This feeds the TNT block to the cube.
steps.success_cue: The Sulfur Cube visibly contains the TNT block and has entered its TNT-absorbed explosive archetype.

steps.action: Do not ignite the cube yet. Re-query the relevant game rule so that its state is confirmed after the entity setup. Open chat, execute the exact command, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The command output still reports that minecraft:mob_griefing is false, and the TNT-absorbed Sulfur Cube remains present.

steps.action: Select Flint and Steel in the hotbar. Approach to normal interaction range and keep the crosshair centered on the body of the TNT-absorbed Sulfur Cube. Make sure the crosshair is not targeting a nearby block, and stop issuing movement or attack inputs.
steps.success_cue: Flint and Steel is the active hotbar item, the TNT-absorbed Sulfur Cube is directly targeted, and minecraft:mob_griefing remains false.

steps.action: Press Use Item exactly once on the targeted TNT-absorbed Sulfur Cube; the default input is right-click. This is the priming action. Immediately stop interacting and hand control to the observation subsystem without attempting to extinguish, shear, damage, pick up, or ignite the cube again.
steps.success_cue: The Flint and Steel use interaction has just been performed once on the TNT-absorbed Sulfur Cube while minecraft:mob_griefing is false; no further player action has been taken.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just used Flint and Steel once on the TNT-absorbed Sulfur Cube while the queried value of minecraft:mob_griefing is false. Begin observation immediately and leave the player and cube undisturbed during the subsequent fuse interval.
uncertainties: The report contains no formal Steps to Reproduce section, so the minimum path was reconstructed from the description and affected feature context.

The report does not specify a game mode, world seed, coordinates, world type, difficulty, or dedicated-server requirement. Creative single-player with commands enabled is used as the simplest deterministic setup and is a practical inference rather than a reported requirement.

The report names the rule as mob_griefing but does not provide a command. Game rules had already been converted to registry resource locations with snake_case names by this version, so the plan uses the version-compatible form minecraft:mob_griefing.

The report does not specify how the Sulfur Cube or required items were obtained. Creative inventory acquisition and a Sulfur Cube Spawn Egg are used to avoid unrelated exploration, crafting, and natural-spawn randomness.

Flint and Steel is selected as the deterministic igniter. Snapshot documentation confirms that absorbed TNT can be primed by fire sources, and related fixes in the following snapshot refer to direct igniter use on TNT-filled Sulfur Cubes.

source_meta._title: Small sulfur cubes become large client-side when fed a slimeball after restarting their aging

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition 26.2 Snapshot 1 in a new single-player world using the integrated server. Use Creative mode and Normal difficulty, with no mods, resource packs, or datapacks. Default mouse controls are assumed: right-click for Use Item/Interact and left-click for Attack. A dedicated server and additional players are not required.
preconditions: Launch exactly 26.2 Snapshot 1, the first version listed as affected; do not use the fixed 26.2 Snapshot 6.
Use a disposable test world because snapshots may damage or convert worlds.
Create the world in Creative mode so the required spawn egg, Golden Dandelions, Slimeball, and weapon can be obtained deterministically.
Use Normal difficulty rather than Peaceful because sulfur-cube spawning on Peaceful was changed during the 26.2 snapshot cycle.
Locate a clear patch of solid ground with enough room for the sulfur cubes to hop apart.
Do not feed or insert any block into the sulfur cube during setup.
Perform both Golden Dandelion interactions and the Slimeball interaction on the same small sulfur cube.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, start the installation whose version is exactly "26.2 Snapshot 1".
steps.exact_input: Minecraft Launcher -> Installations -> select/create an installation using 26.2 Snapshot 1 -> Play
steps.success_cue: The Java Edition title screen finishes loading and displays version 26.2 Snapshot 1.

steps.action: Create a new single-player Creative-mode test world. Set the difficulty to Normal; the seed and world-generation type may remain at their defaults.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Difficulty: Normal -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player enters a new world in Creative mode.

steps.action: Wait for initial world loading to finish before preparing the test.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain is rendered, the loading overlay is gone, and player movement responds normally.

steps.action: Move to a clear area of solid ground with approximately 8 by 8 blocks of open space. If necessary, double-tap the Jump control to begin Creative flight and search nearby, then land before spawning the mob.
steps.exact_input: Default controls: W/A/S/D to move; double-tap Space to toggle Creative flight
steps.success_cue: The player is standing near a clear, solid area where multiple sulfur cubes can be seen and individually targeted.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory and select the Search Items tab so items can be found by name.
steps.exact_input: Press E, then select Search Items
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory is open with an active item-search field.

steps.action: Search for "Sulfur Cube Spawn Egg" and place one in hotbar slot 1, the leftmost inventory bar slot.
steps.exact_input: Search: Sulfur Cube Spawn Egg; place the result in hotbar slot 1
steps.success_cue: A Sulfur Cube Spawn Egg is visible in hotbar slot 1.

steps.action: Search for "Golden Dandelion" and place a stack containing at least two in hotbar slot 2. In Creative mode the stack may not decrease, but two separate interactions must still be performed.
steps.exact_input: Search: Golden Dandelion; place the result in hotbar slot 2
steps.success_cue: Golden Dandelions are visible in hotbar slot 2.

steps.action: Search for "Slimeball" and place one or more Slimeballs in hotbar slot 3.
steps.exact_input: Search: Slimeball; place the result in hotbar slot 3
steps.success_cue: A Slimeball stack is visible in hotbar slot 3.

steps.action: Search for "Netherite Sword" and place one in hotbar slot 4. The sword is used only to produce small sulfur cubes from a newly spawned large cube.
steps.exact_input: Search: Netherite Sword; place the result in hotbar slot 4
steps.success_cue: A Netherite Sword is visible in hotbar slot 4, and all four required hotbar items are prepared.

steps.action: Close the inventory and return to normal world control.
steps.success_cue: The inventory closes and the crosshair is visible.

steps.action: Select hotbar slot 1 so the Sulfur Cube Spawn Egg is held in the active slot.
steps.success_cue: The player's hand displays the Sulfur Cube Spawn Egg and hotbar slot 1 is highlighted.

steps.action: Aim at the top surface of the clear ground and use the spawn egg once to spawn a sulfur cube.
steps.success_cue: One large sulfur cube without an absorbed block is present near the player.

steps.action: Select the Netherite Sword in hotbar slot 4.
steps.success_cue: The player's hand displays the Netherite Sword and hotbar slot 4 is highlighted.

steps.action: Aim directly at the newly spawned large sulfur cube and attack it until it dies. Do not attack either of the resulting small cubes.
steps.exact_input: Left-click the large sulfur cube repeatedly until it dies
steps.success_cue: The large sulfur cube is gone and has split into two visibly smaller sulfur cubes.

steps.action: Wait only until the two small sulfur cubes hop far enough apart to target one unambiguously. If necessary, reposition so one cube is closer to the crosshair than its sibling; do not wait for either cube to grow naturally.
steps.exact_input: Use W/A/S/D as needed; do not use an item yet
steps.success_cue: One chosen small sulfur cube can be targeted without the crosshair intersecting the other cube.

steps.action: Designate the isolated small sulfur cube as the test target. Keep it in view and use this same cube for every remaining interaction.
steps.exact_input: Center the crosshair on one small sulfur cube
steps.success_cue: The crosshair is centered on one identifiable small sulfur cube, with the sibling outside the immediate interaction line.

steps.action: Select the Golden Dandelion stack in hotbar slot 2 while continuing to track the chosen small sulfur cube.
steps.success_cue: A Golden Dandelion is held in the player's hand and the chosen small sulfur cube remains in view.

steps.action: Feed the chosen small sulfur cube the first Golden Dandelion to stop its aging. Perform exactly one interaction and do not accidentally interact with its sibling.
steps.exact_input: Right-click the chosen small sulfur cube once
steps.success_cue: The Golden Dandelion interaction registers on the chosen cube, indicated by the stop-aging particle response around that cube; it remains visibly small.

steps.action: While still holding the Golden Dandelion, feed the same small sulfur cube a second time to restart its aging. Do not wait for natural growth after this interaction.
steps.exact_input: Right-click the same small sulfur cube once more
steps.success_cue: A second, restart-aging particle response appears around the same cube, and the target is still small at the end of the interaction.

steps.action: Immediately select the Slimeball in hotbar slot 3, keeping the same recently restarted sulfur cube under the crosshair.
steps.success_cue: A Slimeball is held in the player's hand and the same small sulfur cube is still targeted.

steps.action: Immediately feed that same sulfur cube one Slimeball. Perform no further movement, inventory action, feeding, reloading, or interaction after the feed registers.
steps.exact_input: Right-click the same small sulfur cube once
steps.success_cue: The Slimeball feeding interaction has just registered on the target cube, such as through the use animation or feeding particles; input stops immediately for observation handoff.

stor.handoff_condition: The same small sulfur cube has just been fed one Slimeball immediately after its aging was first stopped and then restarted with two consecutive Golden Dandelion interactions. No world reload or additional interaction has occurred; begin observing the target's client-side appearance and state now.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode, difficulty, world seed, coordinates, or world-generation type. Creative mode, Normal difficulty, and a new default world are practical choices for deterministic setup.

The report says to summon a small sulfur cube but provides no summon command, NBT, or other direct small-cube creation method. To avoid inventing version-sensitive command data, this plan spawns a normal sulfur cube with its Creative spawn egg and kills it; official information for the affected snapshot states that a killed sulfur cube splits into two smaller sulfur cubes.

Creative mode may prevent the Golden Dandelion or Slimeball stack count from decreasing. Each feeding instruction therefore depends on a distinct registered right-click interaction and its particles rather than item consumption.
Two small sulfur cubes result from killing the large cube. Only one must receive the two Golden Dandelion interactions and the final Slimeball; the other cube is not part of the reproduction.

The report does not provide a required delay between restarting aging and feeding the Slimeball. The plan performs the Slimeball interaction immediately to prevent natural aging from changing the setup.

source_meta.issue links: Relates:inward:MC-307684:Named sulfur cubes can despawn after being picked up with a bucket and replaced

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft: Java Edition 26.2 Snapshot 6 in a new local single-player Creative-mode world, with one player, no third-party mods or data packs, and Simulation Distance set to at least 12 chunks. Use the Creative-inventory sulfur cube bucket rather than Snapshot 7 or any later version.
preconditions: Create a disposable test world because the affected version is a snapshot; do not use an important existing world.
Confirm that the running game version is exactly 26.2 Snapshot 6. Do not reproduce in fix version 26.2 Snapshot 7.
Use a single-player world so that no second player remains near the sulfur cube and prevents the required distance condition.
The player must be in Creative mode so the sulfur cube bucket can be obtained from the Creative inventory and the player can fly.

Set Simulation Distance to at least 12 chunks before placing the sulfur cube. This permits the player to move more than 128 blocks away while the release area can remain simulated long enough for a despawn check.
Use a fresh sulfur cube bucket and do not give the released sulfur cube any other persistence condition: do not name it, place it in a vehicle, or interact with it using a block after release.

Use default controls where stated, or the currently bound equivalent: E for inventory, F3 for debug information, Space twice for Creative flight, W for forward movement, and right-click for Use Item/Place.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, open Minecraft: Java Edition, enable snapshot versions under Installations if necessary, create or select an installation for exactly 26.2 Snapshot 6, and launch it. Do not select 26.2 Snapshot 7.
steps.success_cue: The game reaches the main menu and its displayed version identifies 26.2 Snapshot 6.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, create a new disposable world, set Game Mode to Creative, and enter the world. The seed, difficulty, and world type are not specified by the report and may remain at their defaults.
steps.success_cue: The player is in a newly loaded Creative-mode world and can begin flying by pressing Space twice.

steps.action: Press Esc, open Options, open Video Settings, and set Simulation Distance to 12 chunks or higher. Apply the setting and return to the world.
steps.success_cue: The Video Settings screen shows Simulation Distance at 12 chunks or higher, and the player has returned to normal world control.

steps.action: Move to a level, unobstructed area with enough room to construct a small holding pen. Wait until the nearby terrain has rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: A level test area is loaded, with no immediate hazards or existing mobs occupying the intended release point.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Open Search Items, enter "glass", and move plain Glass to an empty hotbar slot. Close the inventory with E.
steps.success_cue: Plain Glass is present in a hotbar slot and the inventory is closed.

steps.action: Select the Glass and construct an open-topped holding pen on the level ground: make a complete 7-by-7-block outer perimeter and stack the perimeter three blocks high, producing an enclosed 5-by-5-block interior with no doorway. Do not place a roof. Creative flight can be used to enter or leave over the wall.
steps.success_cue: The test area contains an empty open-topped pen with a 5-by-5 interior, three-block-high walls, and no ground-level exits.

steps.action: Enter the pen from above and stand near its center. Press F3 and record the integer coordinates shown on the debug overlay's Block line as X0, Y0, and Z0. These are the return coordinates. Close the debug overlay by pressing F3 again if it obstructs inventory use.
steps.success_cue: The center coordinates X0, Y0, and Z0 have been recorded, and the player remains inside the pen.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Open Search Items and enter "sulfur cube". Identify the bucket item containing a sulfur cube, move one copy to an empty hotbar slot, and close the inventory. Do not select a sulfur cube spawn egg or an ordinary empty bucket.
steps.success_cue: A sulfur cube bucket is present in the hotbar, and the inventory is closed.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing the sulfur cube bucket. Remain inside the pen and aim the crosshair at the top face of the ground block near the center coordinates recorded in step 7.
steps.success_cue: The sulfur cube bucket is visibly held in the player's active hand, and the crosshair points at the pen floor near X0, Z0.

steps.action: Right-click once, using the sulfur cube bucket on the targeted floor block to place its sulfur cube. Do not right-click the cube again and do not give it a block, name, or vehicle.
steps.success_cue: Exactly one sulfur cube is visible inside the closed pen, and the used hotbar slot now contains the resulting empty bucket rather than the filled sulfur cube bucket.

steps.action: Press Space twice to begin Creative flight, rise over the pen wall, and hover approximately 10 to 20 blocks above the release area. Open the F3 overlay and rotate until its Facing line reports east, toward positive X. Keep the recorded Z0 approximately unchanged during the outbound flight.
steps.success_cue: The player is airborne above or beside the pen, the F3 overlay reports an east/positive-X heading, and X0 and Z0 remain recorded for the return trip.

steps.action: Hold W to fly east while watching the F3 Block coordinates. Continue until the current X coordinate is at least X0 + 144 blocks, while keeping the current Z coordinate close to Z0. Stop moving once that distance is reached. Do not use Spectator mode or leave the dimension.
steps.success_cue: The player's horizontal separation from the sulfur cube release point is at least 144 blocks, exceeding the 128-block Java mob range used for this deterministic fly-away operation.

steps.action: Remain at the distant position for approximately five seconds without moving back toward the pen. Wait until terrain around the current position is rendered and player movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: Five seconds have elapsed at least 144 horizontal blocks from the release coordinates, and the destination area is responsive.

steps.action: Turn west, toward negative X, and hold W to fly back along approximately the same path. Use the F3 Block coordinates to return until X and Z are each within five blocks of X0 and Z0.
steps.exact_input: X within X0 ± 5; Z within Z0 ± 5
steps.success_cue: The player has returned to the recorded release coordinates and the holding pen is again nearby.

steps.action: Stop above the pen and wait until its walls, floor, and interior have fully rendered. Center the pen interior in view, make no further interactions, and hand control to the observation subsystem.
steps.success_cue: The original holding pen is fully loaded and visible from above, movement is responsive, and the player has not interacted with the pen or its contents after returning.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has completed one fly-away cycle beyond 128 blocks, waited at the distant position, returned to the recorded release coordinates, and is viewing the fully loaded interior of the original holding pen without performing any additional interaction. Begin observation of the pen's state.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a world seed, world type, difficulty, release coordinates, exact travel distance, simulation distance, direction of travel, or time to remain away. The plan uses a new Creative world, Simulation Distance of at least 12 chunks, eastward travel of 144 blocks, and a five-second distant wait as deterministic practical choices.

The three-block-high holding pen is not required by the report. It is added only to prevent an otherwise present sulfur cube from wandering away from the recorded release point; it must not be treated as a necessary bug condition.

The localized tooltip wording for the filled bucket may differ from the report's phrase "sulfur cube bucket". Searching the Creative inventory for "sulfur cube" and selecting the bucket-shaped result avoids relying on one exact English item-name ordering.

The report permits either obtaining the filled bucket from Creative inventory or picking up a sulfur cube. This plan intentionally uses the Creative-inventory variant because it is the simplest report-supported deterministic path.
